description: The machine-readable discovery document set for agents calling the OpenAgents decision API. Every document describes implemented behavior only; api-catalog.json's unimplemented list names advertised surfaces that do not exist.

documents.content: llms.txt-convention entry point: the project one-liner and links to every discovery document.
Authentication contract: oak_ bearer keys via OPENAGENTS_API_KEY or a mode-0600 config file, workspace membership, anonymous access, the typed refusal shape, and operator-side provisioning.
Versioned route catalog: every implemented route with method, path, request and response shape references, the complete refusal-code map, and an explicit unimplemented list.
OpenAPI 3.1 fragment covering exactly the implemented routes with real request/response schemas and the documented refusal codes.
What an agent needs to call the API — the oak CLI, the oak-mcp MCP server, or raw HTTP — supported versions, and honest limits.
This file — the versioned index of the discovery document set.
General agent infrastructure: target architecture, the three layers, and what remains coding-specific. Predates this index and carries no version field.
Remaining design and implementation work for general agents. Predates this index and carries no version field.

related.content: The end-to-end caller's guide: credentials, asking, batching, exit codes, retries, and receipts.
The oak classify and oak-mcp caller contract.
The MCP server over stdio and Streamable HTTP: sessions, protocol versions, per-request bearer forwarding, the server card, and client configurations.
The implemented admission path, bounds, refusal-code table, and retention rules.
Optional monetary admission, settlement rules, and the conditional balance route.
The target product contract — specifies surfaces that are not implemented; the catalog's unimplemented list names them.
The API group's own OpenAPI document; this set's fragment stays scoped to implemented routes.
The classify route's contract, bounds, and verification record.
